mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY growth > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals a tight labor market, leading to wage inflation and increased production costs, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE < 3.5% does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 2% MoM signals a strong supply-side response, boosting economic growth and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO MoM growth > 2% does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy in a tight labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy in a tight labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the specified interaction does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) below 1 million units signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST < 1 million units does not correlate with subsequent weakening demand.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 250,000 signals strong job growth, boosting consumer confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS > 250,000 does not correlate with subsequent consumer confidence.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 1% YoY and retail sales (RSAFS) are declining, the combination signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth < 1% and RSAFS declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the specified interaction does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.
